title: 400 Bad Request
desc: The server could not understand the request.
happened: The server could not understand your request because it was malformed. This can be caused by corrupted cookies, an invalid URL or a damaged request sent by the browser.
todo: Check the address for typos, clear your cookies for this site and try again. If you were uploading or submitting a form, try again with different data.
admin: Check the access log for the offending request. Oversized cookies or headers, invalid characters and broken proxies are the usual causes.

title: 401 Unauthorized
desc: Authentication is required to access this page.
happened: This page requires you to sign in, and either no credentials were sent or the ones sent were not accepted.
todo: Sign in with the correct account and try again. If you already did, your session may have expired, so sign in again.
admin: Check your authentication configuration (auth_basic / AuthType) and that the credentials file is readable by the web server.

title: 403 Forbidden
desc: You do not have permission to access this page.
happened: The server understood your request but refuses to let you see this page. Directories and files are often kept private on purpose.
todo: Check that you are signed in with the right account and that the address is correct. If you believe you should have access, contact the site owner.
admin: Check file and directory permissions (the web server user needs read access, and execute on every parent directory), allow/deny rules, and SELinux or AppArmor denials.

title: 404 Not Found
desc: The page you are looking for could not be found.
happened: The server could not find the page you asked for. It may have been moved, renamed or deleted, or the address may contain a typo.
todo: Check the address for typos, go back and use the site navigation or search to find the page again. If you followed a link, tell the site owner it is broken.
admin: Check the document root, the location / alias and rewrite rules, and file name case (Linux is case-sensitive). Consider a redirect if the page was moved.

title: 405 Method Not Allowed
desc: The request method is not allowed for this page.
happened: The page exists, but it does not accept the kind of request your browser or application made (for example POST on a page that only allows GET).
todo: Go back and reload the page. If you are using an API client, check that you are using the correct HTTP method.
admin: Check allowed methods (limit_except / Limit, Require method) and that your application routes accept the method.

title: 408 Request Timeout
desc: The server timed out waiting for the request.
happened: The server waited for your browser to finish sending the request, but it took too long. This is usually caused by a slow or unstable connection.
todo: Check your internet connection and reload the page. Switching network or disabling VPN may help.
admin: Tune client_header_timeout / client_body_timeout (nginx) or RequestReadTimeout (Apache) if legitimate clients are being cut off.

title: 410 Gone
desc: This page has been permanently removed.
happened: This page used to exist but was deliberately and permanently removed, and there is no new address for it.
todo: Remove any bookmark for this page and visit the home page to find similar content.
admin: Return 410 only for content that is gone for good. Use a 301 redirect if the content moved.

title: 413 Payload Too Large
desc: The request is larger than the server allows.
happened: The data you tried to send, such as a file upload, is bigger than the server is configured to accept.
todo: Reduce the size of the file or data and try again, for example by compressing it.
admin: Raise client_max_body_size (nginx) or LimitRequestBody (Apache), plus upload limits in PHP or your application.

title: 414 URI Too Long
desc: The address of the request is too long.
happened: The address (URL) sent to the server is longer than it is willing to process. This can happen with very long query strings or a redirect loop.
todo: Shorten the address, remove unnecessary parameters and try again.
admin: Check for redirect loops that keep appending to the URL, or raise large_client_header_buffers (nginx) / LimitRequestLine (Apache).

title: 415 Unsupported Media Type
desc: The server does not support the type of data sent.
happened: The server refused the request because the format of the data you sent is not one it understands.
todo: Try a different file format (for example JPG or PDF) and send it again.
admin: Check the Content-Type your clients send and the types your application accepts.

title: 429 Too Many Requests
desc: You have exceeded the request rate limit.
happened: You, or your network, sent too many requests in a short time, so the server is temporarily limiting access to protect itself.
todo: Wait a few minutes, then try again at a slower pace. Close extra tabs or tools that may be sending automated requests.
admin: Review limit_req (nginx) or mod_evasive / mod_ratelimit (Apache) thresholds. Make sure a shared proxy IP is not blocking many users at once.

title: 431 Request Header Fields Too Large
desc: The request headers are too large.
happened: The headers sent with your request, often because of large cookies, are bigger than the server accepts.
todo: Clear your cookies for this site and reload the page.
admin: Raise large_client_header_buffers (nginx) or LimitRequestFieldSize (Apache), and investigate why cookies grew so big.

title: 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons
desc: This content is unavailable for legal reasons.
happened: Access to this page is blocked because of a legal demand or a legal restriction that applies to your location.
todo: There is nothing you can do from your side. Contact the site owner if you want details.
admin: Document the legal reason and respond with a Link header to the blocking authority where possible.

title: 500 Internal Server Error
desc: The server hit an unexpected problem.
happened: Something went wrong on the server while handling your request. The problem is not caused by anything you did.
todo: Wait a few minutes and reload the page. If the problem continues, please contact the site owner and say what you were doing.
admin: Check the web server and application error logs (for example /var/log/nginx/error.log or /var/log/apache2/error.log) for the exact cause. Look for bad configuration, crashed scripts and permission problems.

title: 501 Not Implemented
desc: The server does not support this feature.
happened: The server does not know how to handle the type of request that was made.
todo: Go back and try a different action. If you keep seeing this, contact the site owner.
admin: Check that the HTTP method or feature is implemented by your application or proxy.

title: 502 Bad Gateway
desc: The server received an invalid response from an upstream server.
happened: The server acts as a gateway and got a broken or empty answer from the application server behind it, which may be restarting or down.
todo: Wait a minute and reload the page. Clearing your browser cache may help. If it persists, contact the site owner.
admin: Check that the upstream (PHP-FPM, Node, Gunicorn, etc.) is running, the socket or port in proxy_pass / ProxyPass is correct, and review upstream logs.

title: 503 Service Unavailable
desc: The service is temporarily unavailable.
happened: The server is temporarily unable to handle requests because it is overloaded or down for maintenance. This is normally brief.
todo: Wait a few minutes and try again. You do not need to do anything else.
admin: Check server load, worker limits and whether a maintenance flag is active. Send a Retry-After header so clients know when to return.

title: 504 Gateway Timeout
desc: The upstream server took too long to respond.
happened: The server acts as a gateway and did not get an answer from the application server behind it in time.
todo: Reload the page after a minute. If you were submitting something, check whether it went through before trying again.
admin: Check for slow queries or hung workers, and tune proxy_read_timeout (nginx) or ProxyTimeout (Apache) only after fixing the cause.

title: 505 HTTP Version Not Supported
desc: The HTTP version used is not supported.
happened: The server does not support the version of the HTTP protocol used by your browser or tool.
todo: Update your browser or client and try again.
admin: Check protocol settings (http2, Protocols directive) and any proxy in front of the server.

title: 507 Insufficient Storage
desc: The server has run out of storage space.
happened: The server could not complete your request because it ran out of disk space.
todo: Try again later. This problem is on the server side and cannot be fixed by you.
admin: Check disk usage and inodes with df -h and df -i, and rotate or clean logs and temporary files.

title: 503 Temporary Maintenance
desc: The site is down for scheduled maintenance.
happened: This site is undergoing scheduled maintenance. Like any service, it needs regular care to keep running smoothly and securely.
todo: Nothing is needed from you. Please come back in a little while, the site will return as soon as the work is done.
admin: Serve this page with a 503 status and a Retry-After header so search engines do not index it. See the README for a maintenance flag example.
